title: introduce-operator-service-kms-isolation-and-audit-adjudicator
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add operator-scoped KMS isolation enforcement and deploy an audit-adjudicator service that deduplicates and enforces tenant-region audit TTLs. No user-facing API changes. Admin config required for private deployments.
description:
Context: Customers and auditors have requested a clearer separation between operator-level key usage and service-account-bound KMS activity, plus consistent, region-aware audit retention enforcement. This PR delivers two coordinated changes: (1) an operator KMS isolation gate that prevents operator-scoped credentials from being used against customer-scoped KMS key identifiers unless a safe-bridge template is configured; (2) a new lightweight Audit Adjudicator service that deduplicates KMS-related audit events, annotates them with tenant residency claims, and enforces TTL-based retention policies per tenant/region.

What changed (high level):
- Runtime: add operator_kms_isolation middleware to the vault/kms client chain. The middleware rejects requests where the auth principal is an operator-managed service and the target key belongs to a tenant-scoped namespace, unless a tenant-operator binding is present in the operator_allowlist.
- Control plane: introduce operator_kms_bindings CRD (private deployments) and a new admin CLI (redwoodctl kms bind) to author bindings. For hosted instances this is implemented as an admin API with RBAC guards.
- Audit pipeline: new adjudicator service (go) that subscribes to audit forwarder events, performs signature-level dedupe, enriches events with residency assertions (region pin / tenant claims), and writes canonical events to the audit store with a retention TTL field. The adjudicator exposes a readonly metrics endpoint and a small control API for graceful replays.
- Tests: unit + integration tests for the middleware, end-to-end smoke for adjudicator + forwarder, and a workload test validating that operator-scoped tokens are rejected for tenant keys.

Motivation: Prior incidents showed operators inadvertently using elevated operator credentials to access tenant CMKs in edge cases during maintenance windows. Separating operator usage and providing explicit bindings reduces blast radius. The adjudicator reduces audit noise and ensures tenant-region retention policies are applied consistently across heterogeneous audit forwarders.

Backwards compatibility and migration: On merge we add a migration job that scans operator key metadata and attempts to synthesize bindings for safe existing usages. Customers with custom KMS integrations are flagged and required to run redwoodctl kms bind or approve suggested bindings via the console. Documentation and migration playbook included.

Notes on implementation details (continuous string): The operator_isolation middleware checks the auth principal type from the request context (operator_service | service_account | tenant_token). For operator_service types we resolve the target key's namespace by calling KeyMetadataService (cached) and validate a binding lookup against the operator_kms_binding index. Bindings support glob patterns for keys and optional temporal windows for maintenance. Failure modes return a well-documented 403 with an error code (KMS_OP_ISOLATION_VIOLATION) so callers can programmatically detect attempted breaches. The adjudicator dedupe algorithm uses a triple-key (event_signature, key_id, minute_bucket) and keeps an in-memory LRU with a configurable maximum TTL to avoid reemitting duplicate events within the bucket. Events are enriched by calling the residency-assertor (local cache + verifier) and attaching region_pin and tenant_claim fields. The adjudicator writes canonical events to the audit store via the existing audit-writer interface and sets retention metadata using retention_policy.go rules which map tenant_region -> TTL.

Review summary and rationale for merge: Security and SRE reviewers validated threat model and failure behavior. Performance impact measured: operator_isolation middleware adds ~0.4ms median overhead to KMS calls in local bench; adjudicator runs as a sidecar/standalone service with <10% CPU at 50k events/minute in our load tests. Migration tooling minimized risk for hosted customers (auto-suggest bindings). Given low runtime cost and high security benefit the change was approved for merge.

review_conversation:
Ethan Zhao: Can we guarantee that the binding lookup won't become a hotspot? Priya: We added an in-memory index with async invalidation and fall back to a cached KeyMetadataService; perf tests show <1% latency outliers.
Sofia Martinez: Need to ensure hosted customers get meaningful upgrade notices. Priya: Added migration job and console flags to preview suggested bindings; docs updated with playbook.
Liam O'Connor: How do we handle multi-provider KMS keys that don't return metadata? Priya: We added a fallback mode that requires an explicit binding for keys without metadata; the migration job flags such keys for manual approval.
Security review (Anna Kim): threat model looks good, but require observability on rejects -> added metrics (reject_count by reason) and a SLI dashboard.
SRE comment (Marco Santos): Helm chart values require a resource hint; added cpu/memory defaults and HPA stanza.
Author response: addressed comments, added more tests, and updated helm/values with resource defaults.
Final: Reviewed-by: Ethan Zhao; Approved-by: Sofia Martinez.
ci_logs_summary: CI pipeline: lint -> go unit -> integration -> helm lint -> container scan. Initial run: one flaky integration test in adjudicator (replay timing) failed; re-run fixed it. All checks passing on final run. Container scan: no critical findings; two low-risk linter comments fixed.
post_merge_actions: deployed adjudicator to staging via canary, ran migration job in staging and produced binding suggestions for ~23 keys. Runbook created and added to docs. Ops scheduled a phased rollout in private clusters over two weeks.
security_notes: Introduces explicit deny posture by default: operator requests to tenant-scoped keys are denied unless a binding exists. Audit Adjudicator ensures consistent retention tagging; retention enforcement is pluggable per deployment. Admin approval required for auto-synthesized bindings in hosted mode.
